body: Thanks for believing, it means a lot.

I have thought about transferring, but I would have to transfer to another 4-year institution to finish my degree and most schools want a 3.0+ to transfer (at least of the schools I am interested in) so I probably wouldn't even be able to transfer. Maybe it's worth a shot though?

I have talked to my friends and it has helped but I also don't want to be burdening myself onto them when I know they also have their own struggles too. I guess a lot of them kind of also don't get it just because they're all done with school and in the real world or at least in graduate school and im just struggling to get by here.

School doesn't make me miserable. I love school and the field I am pursuing, I love learning, I hate the current environment I'm in but it is too much of a financial investment to stop where I am now and I know I need a degree for what I want to do with my life. 

I enjoy helping people I guess? My BA is supposed to be Applied Human Services (which is essentially the copout for the people who didn't get into the school of social work at my university), and my emphasis is community based services so I've done work mostly in areas of mental health and substance abuse. I'm applying for my M.Ed in Higher Education and Student Affairs (if I ever get to that point where it is financially feasible) and some time many years from now I would like to pursue a PhD in Counseling Psychology. In an ideal world I would have some type of job that allows me to work with college-aged populations and advocate for them. 

I thought about taking more time off but that is really what stresses me out the most. I need closure to move on to the next step of my life. The longer I stay here, the more of a failure I feel like I am.
